```spe/prediction-log.md (append to end)
Source: spe/predictions/r02.yaml and spe/evals/results/r02/r02.json. The run had 40 tickets and 5 trials per cell.
r02.yaml has no bands. Close-out applied ±0.05 on rates and ±25% on cost after the run (see F6). A ±0.03 band gives the same verdicts.

| priority_acc | C | 0.80 ± 0.05 | 0.71 | not recorded | miss | n/a |
| cost_per_ticket | D | $0.002 ± 25% | $0.004 | not recorded | miss | n/a |

Hits: 3 of 6. The stop-rule streak is 0 of 3 rounds.

Measured but not predicted: priority_acc A 0.79, B 0.78, D 0.66. Cost A $0.011, B $0.009, C $0.007. Tool calls A 4.1, B 4.0, C 2.6, D 3.9.

The naive guess beat the predictions on category accuracy. Its mean absolute error was 0.030. The predictions had 0.035. All of the gap comes from C.

### Which Why broke

- C, category_acc and priority_acc. The Why was "merged tools cut wrong tool choice." The wrong assumption was that fewer tools would remove wrong choices and lose nothing. The merge hid a step the agent needed. C never called check_status on 9 outage tickets (F4). Tool calls fell from 4.1 to 2.6. Category accuracy fell to 0.80 and priority accuracy to 0.71.
- D, cost_per_ticket. The prediction gave no Why for cost. The implied assumption was that a cheaper model gives a cheaper ticket in proportion. D retried on tickets over 2,000 words, and each retry doubled the tokens (F5).
- B, category_acc. The Why was "shorter prompt keeps focus." The number landed inside its band, but the evidence does not support the Why. B scored 0.86, the same as A. The shorter prompt lowered cost from $0.011 to $0.009 and did not raise accuracy.
- D, category_acc. The Why was "same design on a smaller model loses about 0.15." D measured 0.12 below A. That is inside the band.
```

```spe/failures.md (append to end)
## F4. Merged tool skips the status check

- Kind: agent design (tool surface)
- Round: r02
- What: Config C merged tools into fewer tools. The agent never called check_status on 9 outage tickets. Average tool calls fell from 4.1 (A) to 2.6. Category accuracy fell to 0.80 and priority accuracy to 0.71.
- How to spot it: A ticket tagged outage has no check_status call in its transcript. Priority on those tickets is wrong more often.
- Seen in: r02-C-T17-1..3, from the notes in spe/evals/results/r02/r02.json.
- Fix: Keep check_status as its own tool, or make the merged tool run the status check on outage tickets. Add a code check that counts check_status calls on outage tickets.

## F5. Long-ticket retries double the token cost

- Kind: cost and runtime
- Round: r02
- What: Config D retried on tickets over 2,000 words. Each retry sent the ticket again, so tokens doubled. Cost per ticket was $0.004. The prediction was $0.002.
- How to spot it: Tokens per ticket are more than 2 times the config median. The ticket is longer than 2,000 words. The transcript shows more than one model call for the same step.
- Seen in: r02 config D, from the notes in spe/evals/results/r02/r02.json. The note does not list trial IDs.
- Fix: Allow at most 1 retry. Truncate or summarize ticket bodies over 2,000 words before the call. Log the retry count for each trial.

## F6. Prediction saved without bands or grader checks

- Kind: process (SPE predict step)
- Round: r02
- What: spe/predictions/r02.yaml has point numbers with no band and no named grader check. Close-out had to choose bands after the run. same_as_last_round covers only category accuracy, so priority and cost had no naive baseline. The file was not edited.
- How to spot it: A number in a predictions file has no ± band or no grader check name. A predicted metric has no same_as_last_round value.
- Seen in: spe/predictions/r02.yaml
- Fix: Run a schema check before the predict commit. It fails if any number lacks a band, a grader check, a Why, or a same_as_last_round value.
```
